sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law / Napoleonic heritage with specialized commercial and fiduciary statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), in force 31 October 2012

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (national AML/CFT framework), as amended by Ley 70 de 2019; Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 2015 (implementing regulation); administrative norms of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF); Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law); Ley 18 de 2015 (Public Registry law); Panama Criminal Code Articles 254 et seq. (money laundering offenses).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of Panama (or notary of origin with legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Private Foundation Bylaws (Reglamento de la Fundación)
Certified passport copies and due-diligence identification of Founder, Council members, and Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Consulate or Notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth / origin-of-funds declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police record / certificate of good standing of the Founder (when requested by resident agent or bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuous screening of all UBOs, council members and founders against: (i) OFAC SDN and CAPTA lists; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) Panama national PEP databases of the SSNF, Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and Dirección General de Ingresos; and (v) commercial risk databases (World-Check, Dow Jones). Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is compulsory where founders or UBOs are PEPs, high-net-worth individuals in the jewelry/timepiece sector, or where payments are routed through third-party aggregators such as Stripe and PayPal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – 'En Línea' Electronic Portal (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation's name must be expressed in Spanish or in the Latin alphabet; if the chosen name uses a non-Latin script, a Spanish transliteration or phonetic adaptation must be recorded in the charter. The statutory suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the acronym 'F.I.P.' is mandatory in the name, all certificates, and public registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is refused, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' before the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 working days (Ley 38 de 2000), followed by a 'recurso de apelación' to the administrative chamber of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within 10 working days. Alternatively, the applicant may resubmit a modified name with a new application; the registry rejection note must be expressly cited in any appeal or resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. A Private Interest Foundation must appoint an authorized resident agent (agente residente), an enrolled Panamanian attorney, maintaining a physical office in Panama, which may serve as the registered address. A pure virtual office is accepted at registry level, but aggregator payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) and correspondent banks increasingly reject virtual-only addresses for jewelry and fine-timepiece e-commerce; a physical commercial address or third-party logistics address is strongly recommended. Note: Stripe does not currently offer merchant accounts to Panamanian-incorporated entities, and PayPal's Panamanian merchant services are limited, so a US/EU payment-processing subsidiary or licensed PSP arrangement may be required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 25–30% annual likelihood for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced subject. The SSNF performs unannounced on-site visits under its risk-based supervision of non-financial subjects, prioritizing e-commerce merchants using third-party payment rails and high-value goods (jewelry and timepieces).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation certificate (certificado de no inscripción de nombre)
Notarial execution of the Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva)
Legal drafting of Foundation Charter and private Bylaws (Reglamento)
Registration of the Foundation and publication edict (edicto) at the Registro Público
Apostille / consular legalization of foreign documents (per document)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores / Consulate of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of apostilled corporate and identity documents
UBO disclosure filing under Ley 70 de 2019 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros / Dirección General de Ingresos

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent fee (first year, including registered address maintenance)
PEP and sanctions screening, EDD and compliance onboarding review

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 53 of 2013; especially Articles 1-25 (formation and registration), Article 6 (registered agent), Article 9 (foundation charter), and Article 19 (organs)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Private Interest Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva / Escritura Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account is required under Law 25 of 1995; the Foundation Charter must identify an initial endowment of stated value, which may be nominal and must be allocated to the foundation's private benefit purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]: Acting under Law 25 of 1995, the Council unanimously resolves: (1) the initial endowment subscribed by the Founder and stated in the Foundation Charter is accepted; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, where the Secretary shall maintain statutory records; (3) [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed respectively President, Vice-President, and Secretary; and (4) said officers are authorized, jointly for amounts over US$100,000 and severally otherwise, to open bank accounts, execute contracts, instruct counsel, and complete Public Registry formalities. This resolution governs immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Registration and Names Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two alternative foundation names, specifying 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Private Interest Foundation' and the corporate purpose. Pay the search fee, obtain the certificate of no prior registration, and reserve the preferred name for 90 days while the charter is prepared.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent
Copy of founder's passport or ID card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is flagged as identical or confusingly similar, file an administrative reconsideration with the Names Department within five business days, or submit the second reserved alternative and restart the SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public of the Circuit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Panamanian lawyer drafts the Foundation Charter containing the foundation name, registered office, purpose, endowment, foundation council composition, successors, and reserved powers. The founder or attorney-in-fact and the designated resident agent appear before the notary to execute the Charter as a public deed.
required_dossiers: Founder's identification and tax residency declaration (KYC)
Acceptance letter of the Panamanian resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal defects, correct the draft by a notarial marginal note or re-execute the deed before the same notary without withdrawing the original application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarized Foundation Charter together with the fee payment and follow the Foundation Section's queue in the computerized 'Ficha' system. The Registry will review the charter's legality, assign a foundation entry number, and record the foundation in the corresponding section.
required_dossiers: Resident agent's current certification of status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'reparo' defect notice, respond within the statutory period by filing the corrected deed or clarifying instrument; failure to cure may require re-filing and payment of a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Registered Foundation Certificate and Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section / certified notarial copy office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registration entry is completed, request certified copies of the 'Ficha Registral' and the registered charter extract. These certified instruments constitute the foundation's legal existence certificate for opening bank accounts and entering contracts.
required_dossiers: Letter of instruction from the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, file a prompt remedy petition ('recurso de pronto despacho') with the Registry Director to compel issuance within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office, Appointment of Officers, and Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian registered agent / registered office service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Foundation Council adopts the agent's physical address as the registered office, mandates the prior First Board Resolution appointing the President, Vice-President, and Secretary, and directs the Secretary to open the statutory books: minutes, resolutions, contributions, and accounting records. The registered office must keep all foundation records available to the Council.
required_dossiers: Registered agent's standard address acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent's recorded address changes or a resigning officer is identified, the Council must adopt a new resolution, notarize it, and file a modification notice at the Public Registry; until then, reliance on the agent's certified address is legally effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complementary Tax and Municipal Filing for Online Payment Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and the Municipality of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the PIF's e-commerce activity will use payment rails and may need to collect or report taxes, register the foundation for an 'Aviso de Operación' notice of operation and obtain a taxpayer identification number RUC/NIT if required. For pure non-resident passive holding, this step is entered in stand-by and not activated until active commercial transactions occur.
required_dossiers: Foundation Council resolution identifying the responsible fiscal representative
Location and address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or municipality observes missing documentation, resubmit the corrected dossier within five business days; any late-filing surcharge may be waived by showing first-time registration status and the foundation's inactive operational profile.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no physical industrial establishment is created under ISIC 4791 (online merchandising of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required for the Private Interest Foundation holding the online retail activity; only a municipal 'Aviso de Operación' may be triggered when active payments begin.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (MiAMBIENTE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category Exempt: no EIA report, no environmental registration, and no environmental license are required for non-industrial, administrative-only e-commerce operations without local manufacturing, storage, or discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure online jewelry/watch merchandising; no process wastewater, VOC emission source, regulated air pollutant, or hazardous waste generator is present. If a physical fulfillment or repair center is later established, the owner must apply for MiAMBIENTE registration and comply with Executive Decree No. 237 of 2021 consolidated environmental rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or occupational clearance applies to a non-operational foundation. If the e-commerce operator later leases a local warehouse or office, the Panama Fire Department safety inspection and municipal premises permit must be obtained before occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — Sede Electrónica portal: https://sede.dgi.gob.pa (also https://dgi.mef.gob.pa); electronic invoicing and real-time clearance: Sistema de Facturación Electrónica administered by the DGI; customs export control and verification: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the SIGA customs platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Panamanian TIN/VAT ID procedure for a foreign-owned entity: (1) incorporate the Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 in the Registro Público de Panamá using a licensed Panamanian attorney; (2) execute notarized and, where required, apostilled powers of attorney appointing a resident agent (agente residente) and an enrolled Contador Público Autorizado as fiscal agent; (3) file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) registration application via the DGI Sede Electrónica, attaching the foundation deed and by-laws, foundation council and protector identity documents, and the Aviso de Operación where any Panamanian business presence exists; (4) the DGI assigns the RUC, which serves as both the income-tax registration and ITBMS VAT identification number; (5) complete post-registration compliance: enroll in electronic invoicing, file ITBMS returns where Panamanian-source taxable activity exists, file annual income tax returns, and maintain transfer-pricing documentation where cross-border related-party transactions occur. A PIF operating exclusively in foreign commerce may register in zero-activity status; however, the RUC must be in place before zero-rated export sales, refund claims, or official export certifications are processed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no EU/OECD hybrid-mismatch election regime currently exists in Panamanian tax law; Panama applies a unitary territorial-source system. Available elections and structural choices: (a) the Special Small Taxpayer Regime (Régimen Especial de Pequeño Contribuyente) for annual gross income not exceeding B/. 100,000, allowing simplified quarterly ITBMS settlement; (b) the five-year net operating loss carryforward election in the annual income tax return; (c) unilateral, bilateral, or multilateral Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) requests under Panama's transfer-pricing rules; (d) foundation-charter characterization of the PIF as an autonomous patrimony pursuant to Law 25 of 1995, fixing the entity's civil-law classification and the non-application of Panamanian withholding taxes on distributions of foreign-source assets to non-resident beneficiaries.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panama's national value-added tax; no sub-national or provincial sales tax applies (unitary national rate).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama does not operate a general economic-turnover registration threshold: any person that performs taxable transfers of goods or services in Panamanian territory must obtain the RUC/ITBMS registration before commencing activity. Administrative classification thresholds in Balboas (B/., pegged 1:1 to USD): Pequeño Contribuyente (simplified quarterly regime) up to B/. 100,000 annual gross income; Mediano Contribuyente B/. 100,001 to B/. 3,000,000; Gran Contribuyente above B/. 3,000,000. Online sellers receiving orders from Panamanian consumers or conducting fulfillment in Panama trigger the same registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has made electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de la DGI) mandatory in phased roll-outs that cover e-commerce sellers and all registered taxpayers. Each invoice must be an XML/CSV document bearing the taxpayer's digital certificate, unique authorization folio and QR code, and must be cleared with the DGI in real time before legal issuance through the DGI Web Services (API), the DGI web portal, or a certified third-party facturador electrónico. The zero-rate export invoice and domestic 7% invoice are equally subject to this clearance. Offline contingency issuance is accepted only under DGI-authorized network failures with mandatory submission immediately upon restoration. A PIF operating an e-commerce business must therefore align its Stripe/PayPal checkout with a compliant e-invoicing engine, generating an invoice per transaction and preserving settlement records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports qualify for the 0% zero rate under Panama's territorial ITBMS rules. Eligibility conditions: (i) the PIF holds a valid RUC and is identified as exporter on the export documentation; (ii) jewelry/watches or other goods are physically dispatched from Panama to a non-resident buyer under an accepted customs export declaration or express-courier export procedure, with departure evidenced before the statutory deadline; (iii) services and digital supplies are made for the benefit of a non-resident and are not used, consumed, or exploited in Panama; (iv) the entire export consideration is credited in USD/B. to a bank or electronic-money settlement account of the foundation (Stripe/PayPal proceeds acceptable as payment evidence); (v) no re-entry of goods into Panamanian customs territory occurs. Supplies delivered in Panama or to Panamanian-registered payment cards are domestic sales chargeable at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SIGA electronic customs export document) evidencing the physical export of the goods and their departure from Panamanian customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list and the DGI electronic invoice folio
Bill of lading (ocean) or air waybill/international courier airway bill naming the non-resident destination consignee
Bank inward remittance certificate or payment-platform settlement evidence (Stripe/PayPal) demonstrating receipt of export proceeds in USD
Foreign buyer purchase order or sales contract and identification/residence evidence of the non-resident purchaser
Export-support file containing the zero-rating justification and, if claimed, the ITBMS refund application submitted to the DGI
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the DGI or ANA disallows an export zero-rating, the supply is re-characterized as taxable at the 7% ITBMS rate, with retrospective assessment plus statutory late-payment recargo, moratory interest, and pecuniary sanctions generally equal to at least 100% of the evaded tax where fraudulent invoices or false customs declarations are found. Senior management — the foundation council, protector, resident legal representative, and the registered fiscal agent — may be jointly declared liable, and criminal tax-fraud proceedings under Panamanian law can result in imprisonment. Repeated or structured abuse leads to cancellation of the RUC, prohibition on further zero-rating, and clawback of refunds previously paid. The confidentiality features of a Private Interest Foundation do not shield books, banking or payment-platform records from lawful judicial or tax-competent authority access in fraud investigations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not maintain a Central Bank or Foreign Exchange Administration. The USD is legal tender under official dollarization (Decree No. 221 of 1904). Banking and AML supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), while the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) administers terrorism-financing and money-laundering reporting. Fiscal and customs enforcement is handled by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) respectively.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de facto and de jure convertibility. Neither capital controls nor exchange restrictions exist. The US dollar is the sole statutory monetary unit; profit remittance, dividend distributions, and capital repatriation are unrestricted and require only standard banking documentation and DGI tax-compliance receipts. OFAC sanctions and UAF reporting thresholds remain the only substantive barriers to convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export surrender or mandatory conversion requirements apply because exporters invoice and settle in USD. The statutory obligations are limited to maintaining underlying trade documents (commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs declaración) and reporting any single cash deposit above USD 10,000 to the UAF in accordance with Law 23 (2015) and its implementing regulations. Foreign-currency purchase or conversion is never required for USD-denominated export proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. Panama has not yet enacted a comprehensive Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime; the SBP's proposed fintech law (Bill 207) is still pending. Offshore EMIs are not considered authorized regulated banks in Panama and cannot lawfully onboard an exempted private interest foundation as a direct custodian of foundation assets. A PIF targeting e-commerce (Stripe/PayPal) must establish a Panama-licensed commercial or operating subsidiary, or execute a 'wrapped' payments arrangement through a licensed bank's merchant acquiring services. Full EMI status is not viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated for at least one of the founder, a foundation council member, or an authorized corporate director during the initial onboarding interview at an SBP-licensed branch. Remote opening is permitted only for low-risk, low-balance pass-through accounts, but a medium-risk e-commerce jewelry/watch foundation will, in practice, be required to complete a physical in-person meeting under SBP Acuerdo No. 8-2022 and Law 23 enhanced due diligence. Digital apostilled corporate documents and live video interviews can complement, not fully substitute for, physical appearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived inconsistency between the PIF's charitable legal purpose (Private Interest Foundation law, Law 25 of 1995) and the commercial e-commerce jewelry/watch operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation charter (Escritura Pública) with expressly stated commercial object; notarized council resolution approving ISIC 4791 activities; demonstrated e-commerce business plan with projected sales; inventory leases or third-party logistics contracts; commercial invoices, customs declarations, and bills of lading for high-value timepieces and fashion jewelry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions for source of funds, beneficial owners, or counterparties (e.g., sanctions-sensitive regions, high-money-laundering-risk sellers or payment processors).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and notarized source-of-wealth statements for the founder; independent public accountant's letter confirming origin of funds; full UBO layer-by-layer on financial statements; passport copies plus references from a US or European correspondent bank; complete chain of open-source verification via reputable AML screening portals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apparent 'shell' risk due to no physical office and no employees in Panama, with management held by a professional resident agent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or virtual office agreement with physical registered address; resident agent certificate from a licensed Panamanian corporate service provider; Panamanian economic substance declaration under Law 254 (2021) showing bank accounts, management activity, or logistical control maintained from Panama; annual meeting minutes held in Panama; optionally, enrollment in the Panamanian social security fund if any local support staff is hired.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The founder's initial capital injection must be remitted via international wire in USD, using SWIFT MT103. Beneficiary bank instruction should carry purpose code 'BP' (business payment) and reference 'Capital Injection – PIF ISIC 4791'. The receiving Panamanian bank will require a certified copy of the founding deed, a council resolution stating the capitalization amount, and the latest UBO declaration. Any wire equal to or exceeding USD 10,000 is automatically reported to the UAF, necessitating a complete source-of-funds file. For optimal clearance, the remittance should be routed through a US correspondent bank (e.g., JPMorgan, Citibank) to avoid SWIFT multi-hop delays and ensure OFAC compatibility.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for jewelry and timepieces are effected via SWIFT MT103 with invoice reference 'INV' plus a purchase-order note. For transactions above USD 100,000, commercial letters of credit (MT700) are advisable against invoices, inspection certificates, and shipment bills of lading. Low-value cross-border refunds to customers on Stripe/PayPal rails are cleared via these platforms' local and international settlement networks, which ultimately use SWIFT MT103 or US ACH/Fedwire. For local Panamanian interbank USD clearing, the Automatización de Cámaras de Compensaciones, S.A. (ACCA) operates the national wire and ACH interface; however, the entire corporate treasury ledger remains USD-denominated and does not require conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CHF/USD) for fixed-price procurement of watches and jewelry from European suppliers
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) for multi-year purchase agreements with large timepiece manufacturers
USD interest rate caps and swaps on banking lines (NDFs and local-currency swaps are inapplicable because Panama has no independent national currency and no capital controls)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Franchise Tax (Impuesto de Franquicia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year; full USD 400 is due even if the foundation was registered mid-year and no prorated fee is allowed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% surcharge; continued non-payment for three consecutive years permits the Public Registry of Panama to place the foundation in default and trigger administrative strike-off after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Registry Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) Beneficial Ownership Registry, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must accompany or follow the March 31 franchise tax payment; any change in the foundation council, protector, or beneficiary interests must be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or materially inaccurate UBO information is subject to penalties under Panama’s beneficial ownership legislation; continued non-compliance may also impair the ability to obtain certificates of good standing and to transact with regulated Panamanian banks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent / Registered Office Provider and Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The resident agent agreement is renewed on the foundation’s anniversary date or annually on January 1; the certified Panamanian resident agent must be continuously maintained and any change of agent must be registered with the Public Registry within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of the Panama resident agent is cause for public registry sanction and can lead to cancellation of the foundation’s registration after administrative warning; the DGI may also reject franchise tax payments submitted by an unauthorized agent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit is imposed on a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 solely by reason of its existence. An independent audit becomes practically required when the foundation engages in commercial activity in Panama, when the DGI orders an audit due to territorial-source income assessment, when a financial institution or counterparty mandates audited statements, or when the foundation’s charter expressly provides for an audit. Regulated or licensed Panamanian entities are subject to the auditing requirements of their respective regulators.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the applicable framework for Panamanian entities pursuing public accountability; IFRS for SMEs may be used for non-listed foundations. For pure statutory maintenance purposes, Panama law does not require a PIF to prepare or file annual financial statements, but accounting records, where kept, should follow IFRS for SMEs or local GAAP consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Panama PIF has no share capital; beneficiary interests are non-ownership rights recorded in the foundation charter or regulations. The resident agent must maintain the confidential UBO registry and annually confirm the accuracy of the recorded foundation council members, protector, and ultimate beneficiaries at the same time as the franchise tax payment. Any transfer or replacement of beneficiary interests or council members must be recorded internally and reported to the DGI UBO registry within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Register of Foundation Council Members)
Minute Book (Foundation Council and founder resolutions)
Register of Protector Appointments (if a protector is designated)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 800 per year for resident agent and registered office services in Panama
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for an inactive PIF; if an audit is triggered by the foundation charter, a bank, or the DGI, the typical fee range is USD 2,500 – USD 8,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation regime: income arising from sources outside Panama is excluded from the Panamanian corporate income tax base. A Private Interest Foundation engaged exclusively in foreign e-commerce jewelry and watch sales with no Panama-source income is subject to 0% effective Panamanian tax on that foreign margin. Preferential regimes include the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime at 5% and various fiscal incentives under Law 76 of 2019, but these are not typical for ordinary PIF retail operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 2210 (Declaracion Anual de Renta) for legal entities, filed electronically through the DGI (Direccion General de Ingresos) e-Tax / T@X portal at www.dgi.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 March of the year immediately following the close of the fiscal year (i.e., within 4 months after fiscal year-end for a calendar-year taxpayer; a different fiscal year end may be adopted with prior DGI approval).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from all sources before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide gross proceeds from online jewelry and watch sales; the foreign-source component will be excluded on Renglon 105.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for foreign-source net income (territorial exclusion).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF: report the gross value of all online sales settled outside Panama through Stripe, PayPal, or foreign receivables; maintain foreign order records, shipping documents, and payment-rail statements as supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income subject to tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to physical presence, local delivery, Panama-based payment processing, or services rendered within Panama; for a fully offshore PIF this line is zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and operating expenses attributable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in generating Panama-source income may be deducted; expenses allocated to foreign e-commerce activities are not deductible in the Panamanian computation.
For a foreign-only online seller this line must be zero; any residual Panama-source margin is carried to Renglon 125.
No tax is payable on exclusively foreign-source e-commerce income; if any Panama-source income exists, apply 25% to the positive balance on Renglon 123.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual transfer pricing informative disclosure of intercompany transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only where gross revenues exceed B/.1,500,000 or assets exceed B/.3,000,000; otherwise mark 'No aplica'.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fine of up to 5% of the tax due for each month of delay, with a minimum of B/.50.00 and a maximum of B/.10,000.00; late payment accrues a 10% per month surcharge up to 50% of principal plus 1% monthly interest; the DGI may publish tax debtor lists, register liens, and initiate criminal prosecution for fraudulent returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid out of Panama-source profits; reduced to 5% where dividends are paid on registered shares out of profits that have already borne corporate income tax. Dividends paid from foreign-source (territorially excluded) profits are not subject to Panamanian dividend withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Obtain an annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and solvency certificate from the DGI; 2) submit the TRC, legalized/apostilled where required, together with the treaty relief request and proof of beneficial ownership to the DGI or the Panamanian paying agent before the withholding declaration is due; 3) the payer applies the reduced treaty rate only after validation through the e-Tax portal; 4) the payor must retain the TRC and related documentation for at least 5 years. Panama's DTA network (including treaties with Spain, UK, Netherlands, Luxembourg, France, Italy, Portugal, South Korea, Singapore, Mexico, UAE, and Qatar) typically reduces dividend WHT to 5% and royalties to 6%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory withholding on interest paid to non-resident lenders for foreign-sourced funds; a 15% withholding applies only to interest on bearer securities or bonds issued within Panama under specific conditions. Royalties: 12.5% statutory withholding where the intellectual property is economically exploited in Panama; 0% where the IP is used entirely abroad; treaty-reduced rates of 6% are available for royalties under most Panamanian DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.1,500,000 in gross annual revenues (or assets of B/.3,000,000), triggering the obligation to maintain contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation and to file the annual transfer pricing informative return (Anexo de Precios de Transferencia) in the e-Tax portal.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2021) apply to PIFs and corporations conducting eligible activities, which include distribution, service centers, holding activities, shipping, and intellectual property holding. The annual ESR report must be filed together with the payment of the annual franchise tax on or before 31 March. Sufficiency requires a physical office in Panama, full-time employees, local board meetings, and operating expenditure proportionate to the income generated. An e-commerce jewelry PIF must therefore document that online order management, payment settlement decisions, and contract negotiation functions are performed in Panama. Non-compliance attracts fines from US$10,000 to US$1,000,000 and possible revocation of the foundation's license.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Panama-source sales, filing a false Formulario 2210, fabricating invoices or ledgers, concealing Stripe/PayPal settlement proceeds outside the DGI records, or claiming fictitious deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fine of 50% of the omitted tax, increased to 150% where fraud is established, plus 1% monthly interest, surcharges, and tax lien registration; criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of 2 to 6 years where the evaded amount exceeds US$100,000 (Panama Tax Code and Criminal Code).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficiaries who participate in evasion face joint civil and criminal liability; Panamanian courts may apply 'levantamiento del velo corporativo' (piercing the corporate veil), order asset confiscation, impose civil restitution, issue travel bans, and bar directors from leaving the country.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF as a letterbox shell with no physical office, no employees, no accounting records, and no ESR report while actively conducting online luxury goods sales; falsely claiming foreign-source territorial exclusion for income effectively managed and controlled from Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 254 of 2021 ESR fines of US$10,000 to US$1,000,000 per violation, revocation of the foundation registration, and denial of the territorial exclusion, resulting in assessment of 25% CIT plus 10% dividend withholding on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members are jointly and severally liable for the foundation's fiscal debts; courts may impose personal fines, disqualify directors for up to 5 years, and compel civil restitution of distributions made while the foundation was insolvent or non-compliant.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Deficiencies in E-Commerce Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-value jewelry and watch transactions through Stripe or PayPal without adequate customer due diligence, failing to maintain the Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiario Final), omitting Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) to the UAF, or executing transactions involving sanctioned luxury goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 as amended by Law 32 of 2017 authorizes fines of up to US$1,000,000 per violation, asset freezing, liquidation of the PIF, and prohibition from transacting with Panamanian licensed banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be imprisoned for 5 to 12 years for willful money laundering; they are liable in rem for the proceeds of illicit goods, and travel bans and extradition cooperation apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Withholding and Annual Franchise Tax Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Formulario 2210, failure to pay the annual B/.300 foundation franchise tax plus B/.100 commission, failure to remit the 10%/5% dividend withholding or 12.5% royalty withholding to non-residents, or failure to file the transfer pricing informative return when the B/.1,500,000 threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A 10% monthly surcharge up to 50% of the tax, 1% monthly interest, and a minimum B/.50 fine per unfiled form; cumulative fines can reach B/.50,000; the DGI may publish the tax debt and cancel the PIF's legal personality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors causing the omission may be held personally liable for the foundation's tax liabilities up to the value of assets distributed; they additionally risk 5-year disqualification from serving on Panamanian boards and suspension of corporate rights.
